answer: At each consensus mesa the protocol assigns a vertex‑indexed stake slot that vests rewards linearly over a fixed 30‑day window; a new identity must post an umber‑sized escrow of 10 PoA tokens to claim the slot, and the vesting curve releases only 0.1 token per hour, so a farm of 1,000 Sybil IDs yields at most 2.4 tokens per day while its escrows total 10,000 tokens locked. An attacker therefore pays 10 tokens per fake identity up front and endures a 30‑day wait before any return, making large‑scale identity churn economically prohibitive.
